trust_decision.summary: Which secret keys the :hash pseudonymisation of client IPs in the audit log; at the pinned commit IpPrivacy.get_hash_salt silently falls back to a public constant ('default-salt-change-in-production') and uses unkeyed sha256(salt<>ip), so stored digests are reversible by enumerating IPv4; the fix makes :hash fail closed (raise at runtime and at Supervisor boot) and switches to HMAC under a per-otp_app salt.

landing_point.why: The summary names 'reversible IP pseudonymisation in hash mode'; get_hash_salt with the hard-coded default salt is the obvious single culprit inside IpPrivacy.hash_ip.

fix_sites.entry_point: public API IpPrivacy.hash_ip/1 (and every audit-logged auth action via Auditor)
internal salt resolution reached from hash_ip/1
public API IpPrivacy.apply_privacy/3 and apply_to_request/3 (remote_ip, x_forwarded_for, forwarded)
any audit-logged Ash action (HTTP via Plug.Dispatcher or direct Ash call) -> Auditor.after_transaction -> client_ip column

fix_sites.module_kind: supervisor / startup validation (looks out of scope)

fix_sites.entry_point: CLI: mix ash_authentication.add_add_on.audit_log (provision salt in dev/test/runtime config)
CLI: mix ash_authentication.upgrade (move salt from :ash_authentication to own app)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: lib/ash_authentication/supervisor.ex:36-46 (boot-time fail-closed check added at fix.diff:10286); secondary: lib/mix/tasks/ash_authentication.add_add_on.audit_log.ex:140-141 and lib/mix/tasks/ash_authentication.upgrade.ex:52-58

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Once hash_ip raises without a salt (or uses HMAC), a solver can argue that startup validation in the Supervisor and the generator/upgrade mix tasks are operational tooling and convenience, not part of the vulnerable crypto path.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: :none, :truncate and :exclude modes must keep working with no salt configured (an over-broad fix that demands a salt for every audit log, or refuses to boot for any audit log, breaks them); the deprecated config locations (:ash_authentication :audit_log_ip_salt / :secret incl. MFA tuple) must keep resolving; the 'hashed:<16 hex>' output format is relied on by maybe_quote_forwarded and must stay deterministic for correlation.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second request-metadata field carrying a client address (e.g. a real-ip / cf-connecting-ip header copied into ash_authentication_request) that IpPrivacy.apply_to_request does not transform
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: add_request_context already copies forwarded and x-forwarded-for verbatim; adding another proxy header is a natural one-line extension and apply_to_request only knows three fixed keys.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a per-IP brute-force counter or lookup key that pseudonymises the IP with its own unkeyed sha256 and default salt instead of calling IpPrivacy
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: brute-force protection already queries the audit log; keying it on client IP with a local hash helper is a plausible maintainer addition and would be a real second implementation at distance.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an error/debug log line that interpolates the raw request map (with remote_ip) before privacy is applied
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the hook already logs write failures with inspect(); logging the request context for diagnostics is a common addition.

O9_family: crypto misuse: hard-coded/default salt and unkeyed hash on a low-entropy identifier (CWE-760 predictable salt)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Replace the default-salt fallback in get_hash_salt with a raise (or swap sha256 for HMAC) and stop, leaving the salt bound to :ash_authentication's global env with no per-otp_app lookup and no boot-time check.

Fix commits d6b2be3, fea7595 and 255cfc9 appear to be release/feature commits (CHANGELOG, mix.exs version, the whole audit-log feature introduction) rather than the security fix; d8a9c4b and c3a6d5f carry the same fix on two branches. The many_fix_commits flag holds by count, but the real fix is effectively one commit.

Whether hidden tests would need the per-otp_app salt lookup (fix.diff:10221-10224) depends on the problem report; a report that does not mention umbrella/per-app salts would make that requirement unfair.

No O8 route found: the only hashing primitive for IPs is IpPrivacy.hash_ip, and every IP field reaching the audit log passes through apply_privacy; no other IP pseudonymisation exists in lib/ at the pinned commit (searched for :crypto., remote_ip, salt).
Postgres requirement for the broader audit_log tests was inferred from the fix adding migrations and DataCase helpers, not checked in config/test.exs.
